title: Genome size and cellular architecture
legend: Genome size covaries with erythrocyte area, while nuclear and cellular dimensions are not uniformly proportional. Genome size and cellular architecture in all 24 sampled species. (a,b) Cell area and nucleus area versus genome size, with log10-standardized Pagel-lambda PGLS fits. β denotes a standardized coefficient; brackets give 95% t intervals; P values are unadjusted. (c) Conditional PGLS of log10 nucleus area on log10 cell area. Its unstandardized slope is compared with slope one; the dashed proportional reference passes through the log-scale species centroid. This regression does not identify an errors-in-variables structural exponent. Solid lines and gray bands in a–c show back-transformed fitted log-scale means and 95% coefficient bands; point bars show released measurement intervals. Measurement errors are displayed but not propagated into these regressions. (d) Fractions are first computed within each actual paired cell and nucleus, then summarized as animal medians (open circles) and the species arithmetic mean of animal medians (diamonds). Bars are the central 95% range of 1,000 animal-then-paired-cell resamples. All 42 animals and 1,152 pairs remain. Species follow the fixed phylogenetic display order. Seven morphology species have only one animal; their intervals omit among-animal uncertainty. All cellular traits describe selected large erythrocytes and two-dimensional nuclear and cell areas. Genome size is IOD-derived and D. fuscus assembly-anchored; calibration and staining-run uncertainty are not represented by the plotted intervals. Shared colors and shapes identify recorded reproductive strategy in a–c. Gray diamonds mark the three species with no frozen egg-placement assignment (D. brimleyorum, D. folkertsi, D. ochrophaeus); their aquatic-larval development is known and they remain in every fit. The overview labels a few fixed reference species; isolated scatterplots label all 24. Label choice changes no data or fits. The association results do not determine causal direction. Abbreviations: PGLS, phylogenetic generalized least squares.
alt_text: Four panels integrate genome–cell and genome–nucleus relationships, conditional nuclear–cell scaling and paired nuclear fractions, retaining all 24 species.
